rule_summary: Unless there are special circumstances, at least one applicant must be 25 or older and at least 20 years older than the child.
notes: Ministry of Justice page, last updated 17 September 2025. Section number as cited by Community Law. Govt.nz states the same rule.

rule_summary: A relative of the child can adopt at 20 or older. Relatives here are grandparents, brothers and sisters, uncles and aunts.
notes: Community Law is a national network of free legal centres. Section numbers as cited on its page; legislation.govt.nz could not be read by the project's reader.

rule_summary: No age limits apply when a birth parent and their spouse (the child's step-parent) adopt the child together.
notes: Community Law is a national network of free legal centres. Section numbers as cited on its page; legislation.govt.nz could not be read by the project's reader.

rule_summary: No minimum age for caregivers was stated on the Oranga Tamariki pages read. Its caregiver support policy has a section for caregivers aged 18 or 19 who receive a caregiver allowance.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 12 November 2026. The section is about access to the Jobseeker Support or Emergency Benefit.

rule_summary: CCS Disability Action accepts foster caregivers over the age of 20.
notes: Agency rule, not a national rule. Seen in a search extract; the site's robots.txt disallows the project's reader.

rule_summary: Unless there are special circumstances, the applicant who meets the age rule must be at least 20 years older than the child. This applies if they are not a relative or parent.
notes: Age gap rule. Section number as cited by Community Law.

rule_summary: CCS Disability Action states there is no upper age limit for its foster caregivers.
notes: Agency rule. Seen in a search extract; the page was not opened. No upper age limit was found on Oranga Tamariki pages.

rule_summary: Oranga Tamariki says there is no 'ideal' caregiver: you do not need to be a couple, or even in a relationship.
notes: Stated on the caregiving enquiry form page (updated 25 July 2025). The form lets you add a second person.

rule_summary: An individual (including a step-parent), two spouses applying together, or a birth parent can apply for an adoption order. The law on adoption by de facto or civil union couples is complex.
notes: Section number as cited by Community Law.

rule_summary: Courts have read 'two spouses' to include de facto couples, both opposite-sex and same-sex. The law for civil union couples is complex.
notes: Community Law is a national network of free legal centres. Section numbers as cited on its page; legislation.govt.nz could not be read by the project's reader. Case citations as given on the page.

rule_summary: A person with a partner can adopt alone only if the partner agrees. The partner does not become a parent.
notes: Community Law is a national network of free legal centres. Section numbers as cited on its page; legislation.govt.nz could not be read by the project's reader.

rule_summary: For intercountry adoption, ICANZ says some partner countries accept single applicants, but none accept couples in de facto, civil union or same-sex relationships.
notes: Agency statement about overseas countries' rules, not New Zealand law.

rule_summary: Family Works Southland says foster parents may be single, de facto or married, with or without children.
notes: Agency page.

rule_summary: Oranga Tamariki welcomes caregivers and adoptive parents of any gender, marital status and cultural or religious identity.
notes: 'Ways you can care' booklet, dated January 2019.

rule_summary: A single man cannot adopt a girl unless the court believes he is the child's father or there are special circumstances.
notes: Section number as cited by Community Law.

rule_summary: People who care for tamariki (children) and rangatahi (young people) through Oranga Tamariki must be New Zealand citizens or permanent residents.
notes: Also stated on the enquiry form page. Page updated 13 February 2023.

rule_summary: Permanent caregivers, short-term caregivers and adoptive applicants must hold New Zealand citizenship or permanent residence with no travel restrictions. Applicants must show evidence of their status.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 29 October 2026. The review policy says the status of approved respite caregivers without citizenship or permanent residence is rechecked at each review.

rule_summary: The applicants and the child need to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand unless there are exceptional circumstances.
To adopt from overseas through Adoption First Steps you must be a New Zealand permanent resident or citizen, living and working in New Zealand.
notes: Agency page.

rule_summary: ICANZ applicants must commit to living in New Zealand for the post-placement reporting the child's country requires, which may be 2 to 4 years.
notes: Agency page.

rule_summary: ICANZ applicants must be financially secure, with suitable housing and funds for adoption and travel costs.
notes: Agency rule for intercountry adoption.

rule_summary: Prospective caregivers and adoptive applicants must give a medical report from their doctor. A decision to decline a caregiver for health reasons sits with the supervisor.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 29 October 2026. See nz-nz-fees-4 for who pays.

rule_summary: ICANZ applicants must be in good mental and physical health; how this is judged differs by country.
notes: Agency rule for intercountry adoption.

rule_summary: Caregivers can own their home or rent.
notes: Caring Families Aotearoa, the national caregiver support organisation. No Oranga Tamariki rule on tenure was found.

rule_summary: Tamariki (children) in care should share a bedroom only where it is safe and appropriate for them and the others in the room. Workers check sleeping plans, firm sleeping surfaces and safety-approved cots.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance; updated 4 November 2026 to strengthen the vaping advice. No national spare-room rule was found.

rule_summary: Key Assets asks foster carers to have a spare bedroom in the main house.
notes: Agency rule. Kia Puāwai's interest form also asks whether you have a spare room.

rule_summary: Social workers must assess the home thoroughly. For example, they look at wiring, damp, heating, smoke alarms, window locks, and storage of medicines, alcohol, vapes and chemicals. They also look at stairs, fencing and play equipment.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance; updated 4 November 2026 to strengthen the vaping advice.

rule_summary: Pools holding more than 40 cm of water must be fenced by law, and spa pools must have a lockable lid. Workers also ask about ponds and nearby water.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance; updated 4 November 2026 to strengthen the vaping advice.

rule_summary: If applicants keep firearms, workers discuss use, current licences and lockable storage, with ammunition stored separately.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance; updated 4 November 2026 to strengthen the vaping advice.

rule_summary: A smokefree and vape-free home is an important consideration. Smoking or vaping in a vehicle on a road with anyone under 18 in it is against the law.
legal_citation: Smokefree Environments and Regulated Products Act 1990, s 20D
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance; updated 4 November 2026 to strengthen the vaping advice.

rule_summary: Workers check whether pets or working animals pose any risk, how they are kept, and whether dogs are registered and have bitten anyone.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance; updated 4 November 2026 to strengthen the vaping advice.

rule_summary: Caregivers need a full driver licence to drive children in Oranga Tamariki care or custody. A restricted licence is not enough. The car must be registered with a current warrant of fitness.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 12 November 2026.

rule_summary: Workers check car seats for children aged 7 or younger, enough seat belts, and car insurance.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance; updated 4 November 2026 to strengthen the vaping advice.

rule_summary: In family home care, 2 caregivers look after up to 6 tamariki (children) in a home provided by Oranga Tamariki.
notes: No national limit for other types of care was found; approval can be limited to set groups of children (see nz-nz-licence_type-3).

rule_summary: A Police vet from the New Zealand Police Vetting Service is required for everyone who has a suitability check.
legal_citation: Oranga Tamariki (National Care Standards and Related Matters) Regulations 2018, regs 48, 53
notes: Read in the Oranga Tamariki regulation booklet (V2, updated October 2021). legislation.govt.nz could not be read by the project's reader, so later amendments were not checked.

rule_summary: Suitability checks cover the applicant and household members aged 18 or over. Workers must consider a Police vet and records check for household members aged 14 to 17.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 29 October 2026. Other adults with regular unsupervised or overnight contact may also be checked.

rule_summary: Everyone checked must list their home addresses for the previous 5 years.
legal_citation: Oranga Tamariki (National Care Standards and Related Matters) Regulations 2018, reg 54(1)(a)(i)
notes: Read in the Oranga Tamariki regulation booklet (V2, updated October 2021). legislation.govt.nz could not be read by the project's reader, so later amendments were not checked.

rule_summary: Applicants who have lived habitually in another country need overseas police vetting. If it cannot be got, an extra overseas referee may be used and the report must say so.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance, last modified 15 June 2026.

rule_summary: People vetted to care for a child have their conviction history released, because the Clean Slate exceptions apply.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance, last modified 15 June 2026.

rule_summary: The Police Vetting Service processes vetting requests within 20 working days. Urgent requests take 1 to 3 working days.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance. Sites have a limited number of urgent requests.

rule_summary: Open Home Foundation's Police check includes boarders and other adults over 17 in the home.
notes: Agency rule.

rule_summary: Oranga Tamariki searches its own records (CYRAS, TRIM and CGIS) for everyone who has a suitability check, with their consent.
legal_citation: Oranga Tamariki (National Care Standards and Related Matters) Regulations 2018, reg 54(1)(c)
notes: Read in the Oranga Tamariki regulation booklet (V2, updated October 2021). legislation.govt.nz could not be read by the project's reader, so later amendments were not checked. Record system names from the Practice Centre policy.

rule_summary: Each person checked names at least 2 referees who have known them for 2 years. One is not related to them and one is from their extended family. Oranga Tamariki contacts at least 2.
legal_citation: Oranga Tamariki (National Care Standards and Related Matters) Regulations 2018, reg 54(1)(a)(ii), 54(2)
notes: Read in the Oranga Tamariki regulation booklet (V2, updated October 2021). legislation.govt.nz could not be read by the project's reader, so later amendments were not checked. The 2-year rule and the need for one referee who knows the household as a group come from the Practice Centre policy.

rule_summary: The assessment must look at experience, skills (including cultural competence) and attitudes. It must also look at the home's safety, the household's needs and strengths, support needs and the likely effects of a placement.
legal_citation: Oranga Tamariki (National Care Standards and Related Matters) Regulations 2018, regs 46, 56
notes: Read in the Oranga Tamariki regulation booklet (V2, updated October 2021). legislation.govt.nz could not be read by the project's reader, so later amendments were not checked.

rule_summary: A social worker meets you at home to talk about your experience and strengths. They also talk about your ability to support oranga (wellbeing) and to nurture different cultures. Other topics are the safety of your home and vehicle, and support needs.
notes: Public page updated 14 February 2023.

rule_summary: A Caregiver Recruitment and Support social worker leads a caregiver assessment; an adoption social worker leads an adoptive applicant assessment. The worker writes a report with a recommendation.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 29 October 2026.

rule_summary: For intercountry adoption, a social worker writes a Home Study Assessment Report to the chosen country's requirements. The New Zealand Central Authority approves it before it is sent overseas.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance, last modified 15 December 2020.

rule_summary: Domestic adoptive applicants have several interviews with social workers. Once approved, they prepare a family profile that birth parents use to choose adoptive parents.
notes: Public page updated 15 November 2023.

rule_summary: People who express interest are invited to an Exploring Care information session. They get an application pack and an Exploring Care workbook.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance dated 2019; the public 'Becoming a caregiver' page (2023) names a 'Prepare to Care' programme instead, so programme names may have changed.

rule_summary: After applying, applicants must attend the 2-day Ways to Care preparation programme.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance dated 2019; the public 'Becoming a caregiver' page (2023) names a 'Prepare to Care' programme instead, so programme names may have changed.

rule_summary: Before approval, caregivers and adoptive parents must attend the 1-day Safe Caring programme.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance dated 2019; the public 'Becoming a caregiver' page (2023) names a 'Prepare to Care' programme instead, so programme names may have changed.

rule_summary: Intercountry adoption applicants also attend a 1-day intercountry adoption workshop.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance dated 2019; the public 'Becoming a caregiver' page (2023) names a 'Prepare to Care' programme instead, so programme names may have changed.

rule_summary: All caregivers can take part in the Prepare to Care programme, tailored to their needs.
notes: Public page updated 14 February 2023. The caregiver support policy says provisionally approved caregivers must receive the Prepare to Care information.

rule_summary: After applying, adoptive applicants are invited to an adoption education and preparation programme.
notes: Public page updated 15 November 2023.

rule_summary: Open Home Foundation foster parents start with 21 hours of induction training, compulsory for both carers in a couple.
notes: Agency rule.

rule_summary: Reconnect's whānau (family) caregivers do a one-day induction and two days of Crisis Prevention Institute training.
notes: Agency rule for its Care & Therapy programme.

rule_summary: Each caregiver's support plan must describe the training they will get, taking account of training already done, and is reviewed regularly.
legal_citation: Oranga Tamariki (National Care Standards and Related Matters) Regulations 2018, regs 60, 61
notes: Read in the Oranga Tamariki regulation booklet (V2, updated October 2021). legislation.govt.nz could not be read by the project's reader, so later amendments were not checked.

rule_summary: Caregivers must be encouraged and supported to take part in learning and to meet other caregivers. Training for caregivers of care partners is the care partner's job.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 12 November 2026.

rule_summary: Applicants can be approved for one or more types of care. The types are respite, short-term (formerly transitional), permanent (home for life), family home care, domestic adoption and intercountry adoption.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance, last modified 1 April 2019.

rule_summary: Organisations approved as care partners under section 396 assess and approve their own caregivers. Approval requires meeting the National Care Standards and social sector accreditation monitored by Te Kāhui Kāhu (the social services accreditation body).
notes: Public page published 30 October 2023. The Oranga Tamariki assessment policy does not apply to care partners' caregivers.

rule_summary: A caregiver may be approved only for set groups of children, for example one child, an age range or a gender. Conditions are set for each type of care.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 29 October 2026.

rule_summary: Intercountry adoptive applicants can be approved to adopt from one country only. The approval states the age and special needs of the children they may adopt.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 29 October 2026.

rule_summary: A caregiver's approval must be reviewed every 2 years. A review can also happen at any time, for example after a significant change.
legal_citation: Oranga Tamariki (National Care Standards and Related Matters) Regulations 2018, reg 50
notes: Read in the Oranga Tamariki regulation booklet (V2, updated October 2021). legislation.govt.nz could not be read by the project's reader, so later amendments were not checked.

rule_summary: A review includes a face-to-face meeting at home with each caregiver, updated suitability checks and a report approved by a supervisor.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 27 June 2025.

rule_summary: A full review is also needed after a significant change in the household. The same applies after a request to change the type of approval, or an investigation of an allegation of harm.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 27 June 2025.

rule_summary: If a review recommends revoking approval, the caregiver is told in person and gets a letter with reasons. They have 10 working days to comment or correct information.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 27 June 2025.

rule_summary: Approved adoptive applicants are reviewed every 2 years while they wait for a placement.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance, last modified 1 April 2019.

rule_summary: Oranga Tamariki must finish the caregiver assessment and approval within 60 calendar days (42 working days). The time limit starts when the applicant confirms they want a full assessment.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 29 October 2026. If missed, the reason must be recorded.

rule_summary: Oranga Tamariki must finish the adoptive applicant assessment and approval within 90 calendar days of the applicant confirming they want a full assessment.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 29 October 2026.

rule_summary: Oranga Tamariki's booklet says the application process usually takes about two or three months.
notes: 'Ways you can care' booklet, dated January 2019. Caring Families Aotearoa gives the same estimate.

rule_summary: Intercountry adoption timeframes are unpredictable because each country's requirements differ.
notes: Public page updated 18 August 2023.

rule_summary: Whānau (family) caregivers can only be approved for respite, short-term or permanent care.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance, last modified 1 April 2019.

rule_summary: Whānau caregivers can be approved only if they take part in the preparation learning. It can be delivered flexibly, for example on a marae, at home or one-to-one.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance dated 2019; the public 'Becoming a caregiver' page (2023) names a 'Prepare to Care' programme instead, so programme names may have changed.

rule_summary: Support for caregivers must be given to whānau caregivers as well as other caregivers.
legal_citation: Oranga Tamariki (National Care Standards and Related Matters) Regulations 2018, reg 62(4)(b)
notes: Read in the Oranga Tamariki regulation booklet (V2, updated October 2021). legislation.govt.nz could not be read by the project's reader, so later amendments were not checked.

rule_summary: Oranga Tamariki's priority is a caregiver from the child's wider whānau (family) or community. One way is through Whānau Care partnerships with iwi (tribes) and Māori providers.
notes: Public page updated 13 February 2023.

rule_summary: In an urgent placement a caregiver can get provisional approval after identity, Police and records checks, an interview and usually a home visit. The full assessment must follow within 30 working days, or approval lapses.
legal_citation: Oranga Tamariki (National Care Standards and Related Matters) Regulations 2018, reg 51
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 29 October 2026. The regulation says 'as soon as practicable'; the 30 working days is policy.

rule_summary: Special consideration approval is needed if someone checked has a conviction or has had children removed. It is also needed if they have a finding of harming a child, or are a staff member. Serious violent or sexual offences need sign-off at deputy chief executive level, only in extraordinary circumstances.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 29 October 2026. Family Home caregivers also need special consideration.

rule_summary: The caregiver allowance for a child aged 0 to 4 is $301.53 a week.
notes: Paid fortnightly. Rates effective from 1 April 2026 (Oranga Tamariki caregiver allowance page).

rule_summary: The caregiver allowance for a child aged 5 to 9 is $303.62 a week.
notes: Paid fortnightly. Rates effective from 1 April 2026 (Oranga Tamariki caregiver allowance page).

rule_summary: The caregiver allowance for a child aged 10 to 13 is $327.16 a week.
notes: Paid fortnightly. Rates effective from 1 April 2026 (Oranga Tamariki caregiver allowance page).

rule_summary: The caregiver allowance for a young person aged 14 or over is $350.58 a week.
notes: Paid fortnightly. Rates effective from 1 April 2026 (Oranga Tamariki caregiver allowance page).

rule_summary: Family Home caregivers receive $332.03 a week for each child.
notes: Paid fortnightly. Rates effective from 1 April 2026 (Oranga Tamariki caregiver allowance page).

rule_summary: The allowance covers board, personal items and pocket money. A 4-weekly kākahu (clothing) allowance is also paid. It is $105.56 (ages 0 to 4), $119.68 (5 to 9), $147.80 (10 to 13) and $177.36 (14 and over).
notes: No value given because the project's units do not include a 4-weekly rate.

rule_summary: A birthday and a Christmas allowance are each paid at half the weekly board rate.
Weekly pocket money is $2.70 (ages 0 to 4), $8.70 (5 to 9), $13.00 (10 to 13) and $20.20 (14 and over). It is passed on in full to the child.
notes: Included in the caregiver allowance. Amounts rounded to 10 cents.

rule_summary: New caregivers may get a one-off $350 set-up grant for each child's care arrangement.
notes: The caregiver support policy says it is paid when each care arrangement is organised.

rule_summary: A nappy payment of $29.38 a week for children aged 0 to 4 is included in the allowance base rate.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 12 November 2026.

rule_summary: A standard small-cost payment is included in the allowance for items such as prescriptions or school trips.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 12 November 2026. Amounts differ between sources: the policy gives $11.83; the allowances guidance page gives $10.00 a week.

rule_summary: The allowance includes 40 km of travel a week for each child. Extra approved travel is paid at $1.20 a km for the next 100 km, then 30 cents a km.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 12 November 2026. The $1.20 rate is based on the 2025/26 Inland Revenue rate. No value given because the project's units do not include distance.

rule_summary: A Higher Foster Care Allowance can be paid when a child has additional or special needs.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 12 November 2026.

rule_summary: Since 2020, caregivers keep receiving the Foster Care Allowance for 20 days while the child is in respite care.
notes: Public page last modified 9 September 2025. The same change raised base rates by $25 a week in 2020.

rule_summary: Oranga Tamariki does not charge fees to assess intercountry applicants or write the home study. Applicants pay other costs, such as translation, lawyers and travel, and any accredited placement agency's fees.
notes: Public page updated 18 August 2023.

rule_summary: Domestic adoptive parents pay the legal costs of the Family Court application, including the birth parents' legal fees for signing consent.
notes: Public page updated 15 November 2023.

rule_summary: There are no Family Court filing fees for an adoption order application.
Oranga Tamariki pays the doctor's fee for the medical report of prospective caregivers. People applying only to adopt pay this themselves.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 29 October 2026.

rule_summary: A supervisor can approve when a social worker recommends approval, no one checked has a conviction and there is no dispute. Approval of intercountry adoptive applicants is done by the New Zealand Central Authority.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 29 October 2026.

rule_summary: Before declining an applicant, Oranga Tamariki explains the preliminary decision in person and gives a letter with reasons. It allows 10 working days to comment or correct information.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 29 October 2026.

rule_summary: From 18 September 2025 a temporary law suspends recognition of unsafe overseas adoptions until 1 July 2027. Hague Convention intercountry adoptions are not affected.
legal_citation: Adoption Amendment Act 2025; Adoption Act 1955, ss 3, 17
notes: Ministry of Justice page, last updated 7 October 2026. A bill to replace the temporary change (the Overseas Adoptions Legislation Bill) has been introduced.

rule_summary: New Zealand has Hague Convention intercountry adoption programmes with 6 countries for unrelated children: Chile, Hong Kong, India, Lithuania, the Philippines and Thailand.
notes: Adoption of a related child can be considered from any Hague Convention country.

rule_summary: It is illegal to have a child in your home for adoption without a placement approval from an Oranga Tamariki social worker. This does not apply if the child is a relative.
notes: The page does not give the section number.

rule_summary: An accredited intercountry adoption agency may do assessment or placement, but not both. Police checks, medical reports and referee checks cannot be delegated to an agency.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre guidance, last modified 15 December 2020.

rule_summary: When a newly approved caregiver joins a recognised caregiver support organisation, Oranga Tamariki pays the first 2 years of fees.
notes: Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre policy, last modified 12 November 2026.
